ex: 残業{ざんぎょう}続{つづ}きだったんだ。疲{つか}れてるわけだ。
exEn: You've had overtime nonstop. No wonder you're tired.
note: Presents a logical conclusion from what was just said. Very common in casual explanation.

ex: このペースだと体{からだ}を壊{こわ}しかねないよ。
exEn: At this pace you might well ruin your health.
note: Only for undesirable outcomes. Attaches to the verb ます-stem.

ex: 彼{かれ}は遅{おく}れたばかりか、連絡{れんらく}もしなかった。
exEn: Not only was he late, he didn't even get in touch.
note: Stronger and more written than 〜だけでなく, but shows up in spoken complaints.

ex: 初{はじ}めてにしては上手{じょうず}じゃない？
exEn: For a first try, isn't that pretty good?
note: Expectation vs reality. Great for praising someone's Japanese.

ex: 出{で}ようとしたところに電話{でんわ}がかかってきた。
exEn: Right as I was about to leave, the phone rang.
note: Timing expression. Pairs with 〜ようとした for 'just about to'.

ex: 気持{きも}ちを込{こ}めて作{つく}ったんだから、味{あじ}は許{ゆる}して。
exEn: I made it with real feeling, so forgive the taste.
note: 感謝・愛情・心 are the usual nouns before it.

ex: 今日{きょう}は眠{ねむ}くてしかたがない。
note: Casual speech shortens it to 〜てしょうがない.

en: as long as / as far as
ex: 私{わたし}が知{し}っている限{かぎ}り、あの店{みせ}はまだあるよ。
exEn: As far as I know, that shop is still there.
note: 知っている限り and 見る限り are set phrases worth memorizing whole.

ex: 休{やす}めるどころか、仕事{しごと}が増{ふ}えた。
exEn: Far from getting to rest, my workload increased.
note: Sets up a reversal that's stronger than the listener expected.

ex: 電気{でんき}つけっぱなしで寝{ね}ちゃった。
exEn: I fell asleep with the lights left on.
note: Usually carries mild criticism or self-reproach. Verb ます-stem + っぱなし.

ex: 楽{たの}しみにしていただけに、中止{ちゅうし}はショックだった。
exEn: Precisely because I'd looked forward to it, the cancellation was a shock.

ex: 会議{かいぎ}の最中{さいちゅう}にお腹{なか}が鳴{な}った。最悪{さいあく}。
exEn: My stomach growled right in the middle of the meeting. The worst.
